title: BrainLinear: A Linear Model for Brain Network Analysis in Sparse Tangent Subspaces
abstract: arXiv:2608.15266v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Functional connectome analysis examines brain-region interactions to understand and identify disorders such as autism spectrum disorder and Alzheimer's disease. Existing methods typically use GNNs and Transformers to model the full functional connectivity matrix. However, processing tens of thousands of connections introduces redundancy and noise, increases computational cost, and limits connection-level interpretability. This raises a central question: do we really need complex interaction modeling, or is identifying a small set of disease-relevant connectivity patterns sufficient? To answer this question, we propose BrainLinear, a lightweight geometry-aware framework for mining disease-discriminative connectome patterns. BrainLinear first maps each functional connectivity matrix to a shared tangent space centered at the Fr\'echet mean of the training set, capturing subject-specific deviations while respecting matrix geometry. translated_title: BrainLinear：稀疏切子空间中的脑网络分析线性模型
translated_abstract: 功能连接组分析通过检查大脑区域间的交互来理解和识别如自闭症谱系障碍和阿尔茨海默病等疾病。现有方法通常使用图神经网络（GNNs）和Transformer模型来建模完整的功能连接矩阵。然而，处理数万个连接会引入冗余和噪声，增加计算成本，并限制连接级别的可解释性。这引出了一个核心问题：我们真的需要复杂的交互建模，还是识别一小部分与疾病相关的连接模式就足够了？为了回答这个问题，我们提出了BrainLinear，一个轻量级的、几何感知的框架，用于挖掘疾病判别性的连接组模式。BrainLinear首先将每个功能连接矩阵映射到一个以训练集的Fréchet均值为中心的共享切空间，在尊重矩阵几何结构的同时捕获个体特定的偏差。然后，它...
tldr: 本文提出BrainLinear，一种轻量级几何感知线性模型，通过将功能连接矩阵映射到稀疏切子空间来识别疾病相关的关键连接模式，避免了复杂交互建模的冗余和计算开销。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes BrainLinear, a lightweight geometry-aware linear model that maps functional connectivity matrices to sparse tangent subspaces to identify disease-relevant connectivity patterns, avoiding redundancy and computational costs of complex interaction modeling.
